final_response:
I checked — I can't apply this fix myself. The running MCP server lives on your Windows machine, and none of my tools can read or edit its source: list_files only lists directories, my sandbox can't reach C:\, and no copy of tiatoolbox_mcpserver.py is uploaded here. So the change has to be made by you on the live server, then the server restarted. After that I re-propose, you approve the fresh plan, and the export runs in one pass.

The fix keeps the human-approval gate fully intact. All it does is let an approved plan include the read-only export tool. Based on what the tools returned, the flow is: propose_pathology_plan sets suggested_tools_after_approval, approve_pathology_plan copies those into approved_tools, and require_plan rejects anything not in that list. Right now a nucleus-store request only ever gets the prediction tools in that list.

Two possible changes were described: add export_kongnet_nuclei_to_csv, generate_nucleus_instance_segmentation_report, and list_files to the existing task type, or add a distinct annotationstore_export task type. The existing token remains bound to the old plan, so a fresh plan and approval would be required after a server change.

No CSV was produced.
